podcast.title: Rumored Target of Hole's "Violet" (1995)
podcast.body: Smashing Pumpkins frontman Billy Corgan is the rumored target of Hole's 1995 modern rock hit "Violet," which is "rumored to be a telling off of her former boyfriend." This alleged diss highlights the intertwined personal and professional lives of rock musicians in the 90s. "is rumored to be a telling off of her former boyfriend, smashing Pumpkin's frontman Billy Corgan."

podcast.title: Dictatorial Leadership of The Smashing Pumpkins
podcast.body: Corgan ran The Smashing Pumpkins as a "dictatorship," considering it "his band, his songs," which contributed to the band's eventual deterioration. "While the smashing pumpkins were together, Billy pretty much ran it as a dictatorship. It was his band, his songs."

podcast.title: Formation and Disbandment of Zwan
podcast.body: After The Smashing Pumpkins broke up, Corgan's next project was Zwan, which included former Pumpkins drummer Jimmy Chamberlain. Zwan released only one album before it too fell apart. "Billy's next project was Zwan, a group that also featured pumpkins drummer Jimmy Chamberlain. Zwan, however, lasted exactly one album before they fell apart."

podcast.title: Praise for "Loveless"
podcast.body: Billy Corgan of The Smashing Pumpkins lauded My Bloody Valentine's "Loveless," remarking that it's "very rare in guitar-based music that someone does something new." He also noted that bands within the scene constantly wondered how My Bloody Valentine had achieved such a unique sound. "Bill Corgan, de Desmash in Pinkins, dijo que es muy raro en la música basada en guitarras que alguien haga algo nuevo, y que entre todas las bandas de la escena se preguntaban constantemente cómo habían logrado ese sonido."

xref.title: Billy Corgan's Anti-Moshing Stance (1995)
xref.body: In 1995, Billy Corgan publicly took a stand against moshing during a show in Chicago, expressing that such behavior was inappropriate and unfair to other audience members. This reflected a growing concern among bands about safety in mosh pits. "I and we publicly take a stand against mashing."

xref.title: Dublin Concert Fatality (1996)
xref.body: During their World Tour for *Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness*, The Smashing Pumpkins played to about 7,000 people at the Point Theatre in Dublin, Ireland, on May 11, 1996. Seventeen-year-old Bernadette O'Brien rushed into the mosh pit and was crushed. Singer Billy Corgan stopped the show twice, first asking the crowd to cease crushing, then at 10:00 PM announcing the gig was over due to O'Brien being "nearly dying." O'Brien died the next day from massive internal injuries caused by the crushing weight. Her friend and two cousins were also injured but recovered. "I'm sorry, we can't play on, the gigs are over. There's a girl who's nearly dying. We, as human beings, cannot play up here while people are getting hurt down there."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tragedy at Point Theatre (May 11, 1996)
xref.body: During The Smashing Pumpkins' "Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness Tour" at the Point Theatre in Dublin, 17-year-old Bernadette O'Brien was crushed in a mosh pit and died from massive internal injuries. Billy Corgan halted the show, stating the band could not continue while people were getting hurt. This incident intensified the crackdown on moshing and led to increased legal repercussions. "And then on May 11th, 1996, something terrible happened."

xref.title: Decision to Break Up (2000)
xref.body: In October 2000, Billy Corgan made the decision to disband the Smashing Pumpkins. Despite their status as one of the most important, influential, and bestselling bands of the 1990s alternative nation, the band faced too many problems with their record label, management, and reportedly with guitarist James Iha, whom Corgan seemed to hold responsible for the ultimate breakup.

xref.title: "Siamese Dream" Cover Models Reunion
xref.body: The two young girls featured on *The Smashing Pumpkins'* *Siamese Dream* album cover, Ali Langer and Los Angeles Roberts, were child models who met for the first time at the photoshoot in Los Angeles. They are not Siamese twins, as the title might imply. In 2018, Langer and Roberts, now a nurse and an IT professional respectively, reunited to help promote a reformed Smashing Pumpkins and their tour. It has been confirmed that one-time Smashing Pumpkins bassist Nicole Fiorentino is not one of the girls on the cover, despite a claim she made that even fooled Billy Corgan. "In 2018, Ali and Los Angeles got back together to help promote a reformed smashing pumpkins and a tour."

xref.title: Acknowledging Judas Priest Influence
xref.body: Billy Corgan once admitted that some of The Smashing Pumpkins' sound was influenced by Judas Priest. This admission caused "shock and horror" among certain rock fans, illustrating the rigid tribalism of music preferences at the time. "I recall one time when Billy Corgan admitted that some of the smashing pumpkin sound was influenced by Judas Priest and there was shock and horror, treason."

xref.title: Band Formation and D'Arcy Wretzky's Entry
xref.body: D'Arcy Elizabeth Wretzky met Billy Corgan and guitarist James Iha outside a club in Chicago in 1988 and "muscled her way into the new group, which would later become known as the smashing pumpkins." "The hardcore pumpkins fans were remembered that Darcy Elizabeth Retsky met Billy Corgan and guitarist James Eha outside of club in Chicago in 1988. And she sort of muscled her way into the new group, which would later become known as the smashing pumpkins."

xref.title: Billy Corgan's Consistent Leadership
xref.body: Billy Corgan has been the only constant member of The Smashing Pumpkins since its formation in 1988, underscoring his singular control over the band, as every other member has either quit or been fired. "This is and always has been Billy Corgan's band. He's been the only constant in the group since 1988."

xref.title: Billy Corgan's Continued Presence
xref.body: Billy Corgan continues to be involved with The Smashing Pumpkins "in one form or another," indicating the band's ongoing, albeit evolving, existence. "We still have Billy Corgid in the smashing pumpkins in one form or another."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Bridging Rock and Metal
xref.body: Billy Corgan and The Smashing Pumpkins were part of the movement in the early to middle 90s that "slowly closed that big attitude gap between rock and old school metal." Corgan specifically expressed admiration for bands like AC/DC and Led Zeppelin, contributing to a new open-mindedness within alternative rock. "Then guys like Billy Corgan started saying the same thing. Some of those old ACDC records? Pretty great riffs, man."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Championing Classic Rock
xref.body: Billy Corgan of The Smashing Pumpkins publicly championed classic rock groups such as Cheap Trick and Judas Priest. This demonstrates a broad musical appreciation that defies the traditional "pick a side" mentality once prevalent among rock fans. "Billy Corgan of the Smashing Pumpkins champion groups like Cheap Trick and Judas Priest."

xref.title: Influence on Contemporary Artists
xref.body: The album *Loveless* had a profound and widespread impact, blowing away musicians such as Trent Reznor, Billy Corgan, Robert Smith, Courtney Love, and The Edge of U2. Its influence far exceeded its commercial sales, cementing its status as a seminal work in alternative music and being frequently cited by contemporary bands as an inspiration. "Everyone from Trent Resner to Billy Corgan to Robert Smith to Courtney Love to the edge of YouTube were blown away by what they heard on that album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Internal Dynamics and Breakup
xref.body: Billy Corgan's "dictatorship" over the band, treating it as "his band, his songs," led to the band's deterioration and ultimate breakup by the end of 2000. They played one final show before disbanding. "by the end of 2000, things had deteriorated to the point where it was time to call it a day. So the band played one last show and broke up."

xref.title: Involvement in Professional Wrestling
xref.body: Billy Corgan's engagement with professional wrestling began in 2001 when he attended an ECW card and, after being insulted, had the opportunity to hit one of the wrestlers with a guitar. A decade later, in 2011, he established his own professional league named Pro Resistance Wrestling. This evolved into work with Non-Stop Action Wrestling in 2015, where he became president, effectively serving as their Vince McMahon in 2016. In 2017, he left that league to purchase the National Wrestling Alliance (NWA), one of the oldest pro wrestling leagues globally, founded in 1948, where he also serves as president, having successfully revived the organization. "In 2017 where he also serves as president. That's one of the oldest pro wrestling leagues in the world, having been around since 1948."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Love Triangle with Kurt Cobain and Courtney Love
xref.body: In the early 1990s, a love triangle reportedly existed between Billy Corgan, Kurt Cobain, and Courtney Love. After Kurt Cobain's death, Corgan and Love briefly resumed a relationship. They subsequently broke up but later reunited for a two-year period beginning in 2006, creating "hard feelings" that have since reportedly dissipated. "For a while in the early 90s, there was something of a love triangle going on that also included Kurt Cobain."
